question.text: Two charges $+q$ and $-q$ are placed at a distance $a$ in a uniform electric fleld. The dipole moment of the combination is $2 q a(\cos \theta i+\sin \theta)$. where, $\theta$ is the angle between the direction of the field and the line joining the two charges. Which of the following statement(s) is/ase correct?

options.text: The torque exerted by the field on the dipole vanishes
The net force on the dipole vanishes
The torque is independent of the choice of coordinates
The net force is independent of a

solution.text: The situation can be diagrammatically as, The dipole moment, $$ \mathbf{P}=2 q a(\cos \theta \hat{\mathbf{i}}+\sin \theta \hat{\mathbf{j}}) $$ The net force on the dipole is always zero while net torque on the dipole is not zero.
